title: Arcadia shift field docket
body:
Purpose: quick personal handoff + ephemeral runbook for the Arcadia (night) shift. Use this as the working notebook — copy sections into Confluence if we stabilize procedures.

High-level context:
- Arcadia cluster (prod-us-west-2) is a mixed GPU pool serving small-batch host-model traffic.
- Recent flakiness: sporadic p95 latency spikes after model rollouts and occasional controller restarts (see OPS-4821).

Today (night):
- Known issues to watch: increased p95 on /v1/generate after 23:00 UTC, intermittent 503 from model-worker-3.
- Canary is pinned to v1.14.2; rolling to 1.14.3 scheduled for tomorrow morning.

Quick triage checklist (first 10 minutes)
1) Check dashboards: Redwood Console -> Arcadia /v1/generate -> latency/tokens/sec.
2) Alerts: check PagerDuty -> any active incidents? If PD escalation threshold hit, follow escalation matrix below.
3) Basic health: kubectl -n arcadia get pods -o wide | grep CrashLoop || grep Pending.
4) Logs: tail last 200 of controller: kubectl logs deploy/arcadia-controller -c controller --tail=200 | grep -Ei "error|panic|timeout".
5) If model-worker-3 503: kubectl describe pod model-worker-3 ; check node pressure (disk/ephemeral).

Fast mitigations (ephemeral)
- If workers overloaded -> scale up replica count: kubectl scale deployment/model-worker --replicas=5 -n arcadia (only for short bursts; coordinate with infra if >2x).
- If controller OOM: echo 'restarting controller' -> kubectl rollout restart deployment/arcadia-controller -n arcadia. Monitor for stable Restarts <3 in 10m.
- If persistent 5xx across all workers: toggle fallback routing in Smart Router (console). Steps: Console -> Routing -> Arcadia -> set fallback to "cpu-compat" (note: increases latency but reduces GPU failures).

Escalation matrix (who to ping)
- PagerDuty first. If PD escalation to SEV2: ping on Slack #eng-sre and DM Liam O'Connor.
- For infra/GKE node issues: @Rina Patel (infra lead) -> include node name, time window, recent kubelet logs.
- For model-specific failures: @Jae Park (Applied ML) -> include model id, commit hash, and exact payload that reproduced the error.

Temporary runbook snippets (copy to Confluence later)
- Restart sequence for model-worker pods (safe ordering):
  1. kubectl cordon <node> && kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data
  2. kubectl rollout restart daemonset/model-worker -n arcadia --field-manager=arcadia-ops
  3. wait for Ready replicas (kubectl get rs/deploy -n arcadia) before uncordoning.
- Rolling rollback to last known-good (if new image suspect):
  kubectl set image deployment/arcadia-controller controller=ghcr.io/redwood/arcadia-controller:1.14.2 -n arcadia && kubectl rollout status deployment/arcadia-controller -n arcadia

Diagnostics commands cheat-sheet
- Check open file descriptors on a pod (exec): kubectl exec -it <pod> -n arcadia -- sh -c "ls /proc/$(pidof controller)/fd | wc -l"
- Heap / jstack equivalent (java-based service): kubectl exec -it <pod> -n arcadia -- jcmd <pid> Thread.print > /tmp/threads.txt && kubectl cp <pod>:/tmp/threads.txt ./threads-$(date +%s).txt
- Tail 1 hour of logs for error patterns: kubectl logs deploy/arcadia-controller -n arcadia --since=1h | grep -Ei "timeout|OOM|connection reset" | head -n 200

Notes to self (fragile items)
- DO NOT scale model-worker above 6 without notifying infra (node autoscaler behaves poorly with ephemeral GPUs).
- If fallback routing used, add annotation to incident ticket and revert in morning after root cause.
- There was a flaky cron job that rotates GPU drivers on some nodes; watch for node labels that changed unexpectedly (see OPS-4821 comments).

Open questions / TODOs
- Need a safe automated probe to detect pre-OOM memory growth in controller (file a short spike probe task).
- Long-term: update Smart Router to do weighted fallback rather than binary fallback.

Hand-off checklist for morning shift:
- Paste any incident notes to CONFLUENCE:INF-ops/arcadia-runbook (add timestamped bullets).
- If you used fallback, mark in ticket OPS-4821 and notify product-owner @Gabriel Soto.
- Leave suggestions for next night: was scaling helpful? any noisy alerts that should be muted?

Misc scratch (commands I keep):
- kubectl get hpa -n arcadia
- gcloud compute instances list --filter="labels=arcadia"
- journalctl -u google-guest-agent --since "2 hours ago" | grep -i gce

Sign-off
- Leaving: Maya C. at 07:30 local (added terse notes above). Next oncall: Liam O'Connor.

Rough log (timeline snippets)
- 23:18 UTC: noticed p95 spike -> scaled workers to 5, latency dropped after ~90s.
- 00:03 UTC: model-worker-3 restarted unexpectedly (oom). Drained node, restarted pod, node had 2 driver-rotate cron entries (suspicious). Logged OPS-4821.

End of docket — keep this ephemeral. If stable for 48h, I'll formalize steps into a proper runbook.
